codebook:
# Blind double-coding codebook (LIN-3145), written before any label was seen

Unit: one rule = one directive a worker or orchestrator must follow, located at `file:line`
(repo at LinearViewer origin/main; lib/ is byte-identical to 8f5fe4aa). `signature` is a phrase
the first reader recorded for the rule; it may be paraphrased or split across JS string
concatenations, so locate the rule near the line (±15 lines) and take the directive of about
`bytes` bytes that contains it.

## Field 1: enforcement (exactly one)

- `runtime-code` — some code that runs in production or CI refuses, blocks, rewrites or makes
  impossible the violating action, or mechanically performs what the rule asks. Look in
  LinearViewer `lib/`, `routes/`, `server.js`, `scripts/`, `.github/workflows/`, `.claude/`
  hooks, and the simple-dispatcher repo (a simple-dispatcher checkout beside this one).
  Code that only *renders* the rule text, or only measures compliance afterwards, does not count.
- `prose-pinned-by-test` — no runtime check, but a test under `tests/` asserts that the rule's
  distinctive text (or a regex over it) is present in the rendered prompt/source.
- `prose-only` — neither.

## Field 2: restated elsewhere (yes / no)

`yes` if the same directive (same substance, wording may differ) also appears in a prompt
source other than the rule's own template/file: the other worker templates in
`lib/prompt-template-defs.js` / `lib/prompt-formatters.js`, `lib/prompts/meta-prompt-template.js`,
`lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js`, `lib/prompts/autopilot-manual.js`,
`docs/autopilot-operating-manual.md`, `docs/worker-lane-prompt.md`,
`docs/passage-runner-prompt.md`, `docs/passage-planner-prompt.md`, `docs/runner-prompt.md`,
`lib/proxy-preamble.js`, `lib/proxy-instructions.js`. For an autopilot-kickoff rule, the
handbook it inlines (`autopilot-manual.js` / operating manual) counts as elsewhere. Record where.

## Field 3: class (exactly one), applied in this order

1. `retire` — the rule duplicates another rule in the same or a sibling prompt, is superseded
   by a later rule, or refers to something that no longer exists.
2. `convert-to-code` — compliance is mechanically decidable from artefacts a program can read
   (a section/heading present, a count, a size or diff bound, a CI/tracker status, a label, an
   ordering of API calls) so a check *could* be written.
3. `scope-to-risk-tier` — the rule only earns its cost on high-risk work (credentials, auth,
   data migration, external contracts, large diffs) and is written as universal.
4. `keep-prose` — otherwise: needs judgement no check can make.

Record one sentence of reason per field.
